root_cause: The protected-main authority introduced by PR #3898 still implemented a second Supabase production writer in GitHub Actions. It required secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, but no such credential exists in the GitHub production environment or canonical Supabase secret store. The workflow therefore failed before promotion, while the already-connected Supabase GitHub Integration is the provider-native mechanism that deploys protected production-branch changes.
contributing_causes: Production authority and production execution were conflated: GitHub Actions attempted to deploy instead of attesting the provider-managed Git deployment.
A long-lived management PAT was assumed rather than provisioned, rotated or derived through the existing trust model.
The duplicate CLI writer would have preserved a second mutation route even if the missing PAT were added.
prevention_rule: Protected main is the sole source authority. Supabase GitHub Integration is the sole normal Edge production deployer. GitHub Actions is attestation-only and must never require a static Supabase PAT or invoke supabase functions deploy; it verifies the newest exact-SHA production Supabase App check twice, records immutable source-tree hashes and fails closed on provider failure or newer Supabase runtime drift.

provider_contract: Supabase GitHub integration Deploy to production automatically deploys changed Edge Functions after production-branch push/merge.
The Supabase GitHub App publishes a commit-bound provider check on the production SHA.
